topic: What antenna design considerations optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations?
response: Optimizing ground station visibility in LEO requires a carefully chosen antenna pattern with a wide beamwidth (HBW) to maximize the coverage area.  The Walker star constellation layout, with an inclination of 87.5°, and a specific antenna pattern defined in TR 38.821 (for both S-band and Ka-band)  ensures global coverage.
reference_context: LEO constellations offer global coverage due to their relatively low altitude and reduced propagation delays.  A Walker star constellation layout with an inclination of 87.5° and a specific antenna pattern defined in TR 38.821 (for both S-band and Ka-band) is crucial for optimal ground station visibility.
